title: Chronospatial Computer
description: Simulate a 3-bit VM and find the input that produces a quine.
writeup:
## Approach

A simple virtual machine with 3 registers (A, B, C), 8 opcodes, and a 3-bit instruction set.

## Part 1

Direct simulation: execute instructions sequentially, collecting output from `out` instructions. The combo operand encoding maps 0–3 to literals and 4–6 to registers.

## Part 2

Find the initial value of A that makes the program output a copy of itself (a quine). The key insight is that the program processes A in 3-bit chunks — each loop iteration right-shifts A by 3 and outputs one value based on the low bits.

This means we can build A recursively from the *last* output digit backwards. For each position, try all 8 possible 3-bit values (0–7), run the program to check if the first output matches the expected digit, and recurse. Taking the first valid result gives the smallest A.
